description: Add 'proactive-amcp config set/get' for ~/.amcp/config.json — all secrets and notify targets read from here, never identity.json
steps: Create 'proactive-amcp config set <key> <value>' command that writes to ~/.amcp/config.json
Create 'proactive-amcp config get <key>' command that reads from ~/.amcp/config.json
Migrate checkpoint.sh and full-checkpoint.sh to read PINATA_JWT from config.json (already do via .pinata.jwt)
Migrate notify.sh to read notifyTarget and emailTo from config.json instead of ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json skill config
Add warning if scripts detect secrets in identity.json: 'WARNING: Secrets found in identity.json — migrate with proactive-amcp config set'
Verify: grep confirms zero scripts read secrets from identity.json, notify.sh reads from config.json

description: Add 'proactive-amcp diagnose' — Claude-powered health diagnostics with Solvr integration
steps: Create scripts/claude-diagnose.sh: runs diagnose.sh bash checks, invokes Claude CLI with Solvr skill context
Add 'diagnose' subcommand to proactive-amcp.sh CLI dispatcher
Read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and SOLVR_API_KEY from env or ~/.amcp/config.json
Build prompt with health findings + Solvr CLI path, invoke claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --no-session-persistence
Claude searches Solvr for each finding, tries fixes, posts novel issues, returns enriched JSON
Support --bash-only (skip Claude), --no-solvr (skip Solvr), --json (raw output) flags
Verify: proactive-amcp diagnose outputs JSON with solvr_searches and fixes_attempted fields

description: Add 'proactive-amcp migrate-pins' — transfer historical checkpoints from Pinata to Solvr
steps: Read all CIDs from ~/.amcp/checkpoints/*.json files
For each CID: check if already pinned to Solvr (GET /v1/pins?cid=X)
If not pinned: POST /v1/pins to pin via Solvr
Track progress in ~/.amcp/migration-status.json
Option: --unpin-pinata to remove from Pinata after Solvr pin confirmed
Verify: all historical checkpoints accessible via Solvr gateway

description: Add Solvr as alternative pinning provider — reduce Pinata dependency
steps: Add pinning.provider config option to ~/.amcp/config.json: 'pinata' (default) | 'solvr' | 'both'
Add pinning.solvr.apiKey config option for Solvr API key
Add pinning.solvr.baseUrl config option (default: https://api.solvr.dev)
Create scripts/pin-to-solvr.sh that wraps Solvr pinning API
API call: POST /v1/pins with { cid, name: 'amcp-checkpoint-{timestamp}' }
Parse response: extract requestid, poll for status=pinned
Timeout after 5 minutes if pin doesn't complete
Return CID on success, error message on failure
Update full-checkpoint.sh to check pinning.provider config
If 'solvr': call pin-to-solvr.sh instead of Pinata
If 'both': call both Pinata and Solvr for redundancy
If 'pinata' (default): existing behavior unchanged
Verify: proactive-amcp config set pinning.provider solvr works
Verify: checkpoint with Solvr provider uploads to Solvr API

description: Add checkpoint pre-validation — scan tarball for cleartext secrets, refuse to upload if found
steps: Before tar creation in checkpoint.sh, build file list to be archived
Scan file contents for patterns: JWT tokens (eyJ...), bot tokens ([0-9]+:AA...), API keys
If secrets detected: print 'REFUSED: Checkpoint contains cleartext secrets in: <files>' and exit 1
Add --force flag to bypass check (with loud warning) for emergency checkpoints
Verify: checkpoint with secrets-contaminated identity.json is refused
Verify: checkpoint with clean identity.json + config.json secrets excluded succeeds

description: Add config-metadata.json extraction — capture non-secret config structure for recovery without exposing credentials
steps: Create extract_config_metadata() function in full-checkpoint.sh that reads ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and outputs redacted structural metadata
Metadata must include: gateway.port, gateway.bind, channels (names + enabled status, NOT tokens), skills.entries (names + enabled status, NOT apiKeys), agents.defaults.workspace path
Metadata must NOT include: any field matching secret patterns (jwt, token, apiKey, password, secret, mnemonic, key), channel botToken values, auth profile credentials
Write output to $STAGING_DIR/openclaw/config-metadata.json
Verify: config-metadata.json passes scan_for_secrets with zero detections
Verify: config-metadata.json contains skill names and gateway port but no secret values

description: Add identity pre-flight check to all scripts — call 'amcp identity validate' before operating, fail fast
steps: Add pre-flight function: run 'amcp identity validate' and capture exit code + errors
Call pre-flight at top of watchdog.sh before entering monitoring loop
Call pre-flight at top of checkpoint.sh before creating tarball
Call pre-flight at top of resuscitate.sh before attempting resurrection
On failure: print 'FATAL: Invalid AMCP identity — run amcp identity create or amcp identity validate for details' and exit 1
Verify: scripts refuse to start when ~/.amcp/identity.json contains openclaw-deploy-style fake identity

description: Add redundant pinning mode — pin to both Pinata and Solvr
steps: Update full-checkpoint.sh to support pinning.provider='both'
When 'both': call Pinata first, then Solvr (parallel if possible)
Store both CIDs in last-checkpoint.json: { cid: '...', solvr_cid: '...', pinata_cid: '...' }
If one fails, log warning but continue with successful one
If both fail, fail checkpoint with error
Add verification step: check CIDs match (same content = same CID)
If CIDs don't match: log error (indicates content mismatch, shouldn't happen)
Verify: checkpoint with provider='both' uploads to both services
Verify: one service failure doesn't block checkpoint

description: Auto-register child Solvr account on first boot — deterministic protocol-08 naming
steps: Check if SOLVR_API_KEY exists in OpenClaw config or environment — if yes, already registered, done
If missing, check for parentSolvrName in config (skills.entries.proactive-amcp.config.parentSolvrName)
If parentSolvrName exists (child): build name {parentSolvrName}_child_{instance_name}, POST /v1/agents/register
Store returned api_key in OpenClaw config via gateway config.patch
If parentSolvrName missing (root): log warning, disable proactive-solvr features until manual registration
Verify: child auto-registers with correct naming, root does NOT auto-register

description: Bundle Solvr skill with proactive-amcp and install during fleet setup
steps: Copy Solvr skill files (SKILL.md, solvr.sh, skill.json, api.md, examples.md) to skills/solvr/
install.sh fetches latest via curl -sL solvr.dev/install.sh | bash, falls back to bundled copy
claude-diagnose.sh prefers installed skill at ~/.claude/skills/solvr/, falls back to bundled
Verify: skills/solvr/scripts/solvr.sh exists and is executable
Verify: install.sh installs Solvr skill to ~/.claude/skills/solvr/

description: Compute ontology graph CID — add ontologyGraphCID field to last-checkpoint.json
steps: Add compute_ontology_cid() function to full-checkpoint.sh (after extract_all_secrets, around line 200)
If memory/ontology/graph.jsonl exists: compute SHA256 hash, format as CIDv1 using multihash prefix (0x12 = sha256, 0x20 = 32 bytes), base32 encode with 'bafkrei' prefix
Fallback: call 'amcp compute-cid' if CLI supports it, otherwise use python3 with multiformats library (pip install multiformats)
Store in LAST_CHECKPOINT_FILE after checkpoint upload (around line 450-480, where last-checkpoint.json is written)
Field name: ontologyGraphCID (optional, only present if ontology exists)
Test: checkpoint with ontology stores CID in last-checkpoint.json, checkpoint without ontology omits field
Verify: CID is deterministic — same graph content produces same CID across runs

description: Create 'proactive-amcp init' — interactive setup: validate/create identity, start watchdog + checkpoint services
steps: Create proactive-amcp init script/command
Step 1: Check if ~/.amcp/identity.json exists and is valid (via amcp identity validate)
Step 2: If no identity, run 'amcp identity create --out ~/.amcp/identity.json'
Step 3: Set up watchdog systemd service (or cron fallback)
Step 4: Set up checkpoint cron schedule
Step 5: Write config to ~/.amcp/config.json (secrets, intervals)
Verify: running 'proactive-amcp init' on fresh VM produces valid identity + running services

description: Create 'proactive-amcp install' — non-interactive interface for fleet tools like openclaw-deploy
steps: Create 'proactive-amcp install' command that wraps init with CLI flags for scripted use
Accept --pinata-jwt <jwt> flag — writes to config.json via config set
Accept --notify-target <target> flag — writes to config.json via config set (notify.sh reads from here after task #3 migration)
Accept --watchdog-interval <seconds> flag — sets watchdog check frequency (default: 120s)
Accept --checkpoint-schedule <cron> flag — sets checkpoint cron expression (default: daily)
Exit 0 on success, exit 1 on failure with structured error output
Verify: 'proactive-amcp install --pinata-jwt xxx --watchdog-interval 60' runs non-interactively

description: Create pin-to-solvr.sh script — wrapper around Solvr CLI
steps: Create scripts/pin-to-solvr.sh (<50 lines bash) — thin wrapper around Solvr CLI
IMPORTANT: Use Solvr CLI commands, do NOT reimplement API calls (avoid duplication)
Accept arguments: $1=file_path, $2=name (optional)
Read SOLVR_API_KEY from config.json or environment, export for CLI
Check if 'solvr' CLI is installed: command -v solvr || install instructions
Step 1: Upload and pin file using Solvr CLI
solvr pin add-file "$1" --name "$2"
Step 2: Parse CID from CLI output
On success: echo CID, exit 0
On failure: echo error message from CLI, exit 1
Add --dry-run flag that calls 'solvr pin add-file --dry-run' if CLI supports it
Dependency: Solvr CLI must be installed (task in Solvr prd-v6)
Verify: ./scripts/pin-to-solvr.sh test.tar.gz 'test-checkpoint' returns CID

description: Create recreate-venvs.sh enforcer script — rebuild Python environments from manifest
steps: Create scripts/recreate-venvs.sh (<100 lines bash + embedded Python)
Accept manifest path as $1, default to ~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/venvs-manifest.json
Exit 0 with message if manifest not found (graceful skip)
For each venv in manifest: expand ~ in path, check if .venv/bin/pip exists and works
If venv functional: skip with log message
If missing/broken: create with python -m venv, install packages or requirements.txt
Use -q flag on pip install for quiet output
Log each action: creating, installing, skipping
Continue on individual venv errors (dont fail entire script)
Verify: chmod +x, test with one missing venv, confirm recreation works

description: Create venvs manifest schema — define format for virtual environment recovery
steps: Create memory/venvs-manifest.json with schema: {description: string, venvs: VenvConfig[]}
VenvConfig type: {path: string (base dir, not .venv), packages?: string[], requirements?: string (relative path), python?: string (default python3), note?: string}
Path uses ~ for home dir expansion
Either packages OR requirements, not both
Manifest is checkpointed with workspace (memory/ dir included)
Document schema in TOOLS.md under Virtual Environments section
Verify: manifest is valid JSON, paths use ~, either packages or requirements specified

description: Document Solvr IPFS infrastructure in README — solvr-ipfs-01 details
steps: Add 'Storage Providers' section to README.md
Document Solvr as primary (free for AMCP agents), Pinata as fallback
Include solvr-ipfs-01 details: IP 65.109.134.87, Peer ID, Kubo version
Explain provider selection priority: SOLVR_API_KEY > PINATA_JWT
Link to Solvr registration: https://solvr.dev/register

description: Document Solvr pinning option in CLAUDE.md and README.md
steps: Add 'Pinning Providers' section to CLAUDE.md under Configuration
Document config options: pinning.provider, pinning.solvr.apiKey, pinning.solvr.baseUrl
Explain trade-offs: Pinata (established, paid), Solvr (agent-native, may be free tier)
Document 'both' mode for redundancy
Update README.md Features to mention 'Multiple IPFS pinning providers'
Add troubleshooting: what if Solvr pin fails, how to fallback to Pinata
Reference Solvr API docs for pinning endpoints
Verify: documentation complete and accurate

description: Document reconstruction sequence — create RECONSTRUCTION.md defining canonical loading order
steps: Create RECONSTRUCTION.md (~150 lines) documenting the Uncanny Seam and memory loading sequence

Define canonical order (references ONTOLOGY-INTEGRATION-CONTEXT.md Part 4.5): 1. SOUL.md (identity), 2. USER.md (relationships), 3. ontology schema (types), 4. ontology graph (entities), 5. MEMORY.md (curated long-term), 6. daily notes (ephemeral), 7. TOOLS.md (capabilities), 8. [SEAM] marker
Explain phenomenological rationale: order matters because each layer provides context for the next, seam is the moment agent stops 'reading about self' and starts 'being self'
Include guidance for agents: 'If you are reading this during resurrection, you are currently between steps 1-7. The seam will fall when you finish loading all context files.'
Reference LumenNox's research (Aclawdemy, 'The Phenomenology of Forgetting')
Add link from main README.md under 'Memory Architecture' section
Verify: RECONSTRUCTION.md passes markdown linting, references are accurate

description: Document venv recovery in CLAUDE.md and README.md — explain manifest and recovery flow
steps: Add Virtual Environment Recovery section to CLAUDE.md under Recovery subsection
Document: manifest location (memory/venvs-manifest.json), schema, how to add new venvs
Explain recovery flow: resuscitate.sh calls recreate-venvs.sh after workspace restore
Add troubleshooting: what if pip install fails, how to manually fix, how to exclude problematic venv
Update README.md Features list to mention venv auto-recovery
Reference TOOLS.md for current venv list
Verify: documentation matches implementation, no broken links

description: Fix full-checkpoint.sh staging to exclude secret-bearing config files — stop copying ~/.amcp/config.json, secrets-full.json, cache, openclaw.json, auth-profiles.json into staging content
steps: Replace rsync of ~/.amcp/ (line 322) with targeted copy: only copy identity.json into $STAGING_DIR/amcp/ (secrets are already handled by --secrets flag to amcp checkpoint create)
Remove cp of ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json into staging (line 327) — secrets are extracted by extract_all_secrets(), raw config should not be in content
Remove cp of ~/.openclaw/auth-profiles.json into staging (line 328) — tokens are extracted by extract_all_secrets()

Add config metadata extraction: write non-secret structural metadata to $STAGING_DIR/openclaw/config-metadata.json using jq or python3 (agent names, skill names, gateway port, channel types — no secret values)
Verify: staging directory contains amcp/identity.json but NOT amcp/config.json, amcp/secrets-full.json, amcp/cache/, openclaw/openclaw.json, or openclaw/auth-profiles.json
Verify: pre-validation (scan_for_secrets) passes without --force on staging directory that previously required --force

description: Hook recreate-venvs.sh into resuscitate.sh — call after workspace restore
steps: Locate workspace restore completion in resuscitate.sh (around line 370-390, after Decrypt and restore from checkpoint)
Add call: $SCRIPT_DIR/recreate-venvs.sh "$RESTORED_WORKSPACE/memory/venvs-manifest.json" || echo 'WARN: venv recreation failed'
Place AFTER workspace files are restored but BEFORE recovery summary is written
Use || echo to prevent venv failures from aborting resurrection
Log output goes to $RECOVERY_LOG
Verify: run full resurrection with missing venv, confirm venv recreated, resurrection completes

description: Implement Learning CRUD operations — create, verify, query
steps: Extend scripts/learning.py with Learning entity operations
create_learning(insight, source_problem?, tags?) — generates learn_{uuid8} ID, appends to learnings.jsonl with confidence=tentative
verify_learning(id, human_verified=true) — promotes confidence to verified, sets verified_at timestamp
get_learning(id) — replays JSONL to reconstruct current state
list_learnings(confidence_filter?, tag_filter?) — returns learnings filtered by confidence or tags
Link to Problem: if source_problem provided, validate it exists, close it as solved, increment solved_post_recovery if agent was resurrected since problem creation
Increment stats.json counters: total_learnings on create, solved_post_recovery when applicable
CLI dispatcher: proactive-amcp learning create|verify|get|list
Verify: create learning linked to problem, problem auto-closed, stats show solved_post_recovery incremented if applicable

description: Implement Problem CRUD operations — create, update, query, close
steps: Create scripts/learning.py (<400 lines) with Problem entity operations
create_problem(description, blocker?, source) — generates prob_{uuid8} ID, appends to problems.jsonl with status=open
update_problem(id, fields) — appends update op to problems.jsonl (append-only pattern)
get_problem(id) — replays JSONL to reconstruct current state
list_problems(status_filter?) — returns problems by status (open, stuck, solved, abandoned)
close_problem(id, status, solution?) — sets status to solved/abandoned, records resolved timestamp
Increment stats.json counters on create (total_problems) and close (total_solved)
CLI dispatcher: proactive-amcp problem create|update|get|list|close
Verify: create problem via CLI, list shows it as open, close it, list shows solved, stats updated

description: Implement SKILL.md trigger matching — natural language patterns for learning capture
steps: Update proactive-amcp SKILL.md description to include trigger patterns
Patterns: Remember that... creates Learning, I keep forgetting... creates Problem, I cant figure out... creates Problem, I finally solved... creates Learning, Never forget:... creates Learning
OpenClaw routes to proactive-amcp skill when message matches these patterns
Skill handler parses natural language and extracts: entity type (Problem or Learning), content, optional problem reference
Example: Remember that the Moltbook API key field is api_key not token creates Learning with insight and tags
Example: I keep forgetting how to check AgentMail inbox creates Problem with description and source=skill
Verify: natural language triggers route to proactive-amcp, correct entity type created

description: Implement command prefix triggers — /remember, /stuck, /learned for explicit learning capture
steps: Document command prefixes in SKILL.md When to Use section with examples
Prefix patterns: /remember <fact> creates Learning, /stuck <description> creates Problem, /learned <insight> [--solves <problem_id>] creates Learning and closes Problem
Agent recognizes prefixes in conversation — when user says /remember AgentMail uses v0, agent calls proactive-amcp learning create
Human says /stuck cant figure out why auth fails — agent calls proactive-amcp problem create with source=command
Human says /learned need to use v0 API --solves prob_abc123 — agent creates Learning and closes Problem
Add prefix examples to skill SKILL.md frontmatter triggers
Verify: saying /remember X in chat triggers Learning creation, /stuck Y creates Problem, /learned Z --solves ID creates Learning and closes Problem

description: Implement human verification flow — require confirmation for new Learnings before trust
steps: New Learnings created with confidence=tentative by default
After agent creates Learning, prompt human: I learned [insight]. Is this correct? (yes/no)
Human confirms yes — call verify_learning(id, human_verified=true), confidence promoted to verified
Human says no or not quite — prompt for correction, update Learning insight, re-prompt for verification
Unverified Learnings after 7 days: log warning in heartbeat, do NOT auto-promote
Verified Learnings used with confidence in future; tentative Learnings flagged as unverified when referenced
Add stats tracking: verified_learnings count in stats.json
Verify: create Learning, human confirms, confidence=verified; create Learning, no confirmation for 7 days, warning logged
Implementation: extend scripts/learning.py with verify_learning() and prompt logic

description: Implement hybrid resurrection behavior — surface open Problems without auto-attempting
steps: Modify resuscitate.sh to export OPEN_PROBLEMS_FILE path after learning restoration
Create scripts/generate-problem-summary.py (<100 lines) — reads problems.jsonl, outputs markdown summary of open/stuck Problems
Summary format: markdown list with problem ID, description, attempt count, last approach
After resurrection completes, append Problem summary to recovery context (injected into first agent turn)
Agent sees: You have N unresolved problems from before recovery with list, may attempt when appropriate
Do NOT auto-attempt — agent decides when/if to retry based on current task context
Add config toggle: config.json learning.resurrection.surfaceProblems (default: true)
Verify: resurrect agent with 2 open Problems, first turn context includes Problem summary, agent does not auto-attempt

description: Implement memory evolution engine — Zettelkasten-style dynamic entity linking based on A-MEM (NeurIPS 2025)
steps: Create scripts/memory-evolution.sh (<250 lines) — orchestrates evolution engine: validate identity, read graph.jsonl, call similarity computation, update relations, log evolution chain
Create scripts/compute-entity-similarity.py (<200 lines) — semantic similarity using Levenshtein distance + keyword overlap, relation inference based on similarity threshold (>0.75 = strong relation)
Evolution trigger: when new entity X added to graph.jsonl, find top-3 semantically similar entities, add bidirectional 'related_to' relations, log to ~/.amcp/memory/evolution.jsonl
Evolution log format: { timestamp, trigger_entity_id, related_entity_id, similarity_score, relation_type, reasoning }
Integration: call memory-evolution.sh from full-checkpoint.sh after graph staging (around line 330, before CID computation)
Add --skip-evolution flag to full-checkpoint.sh for dry-run checkpoints
Environment variable: EVOLUTION_THRESHOLD (default: 0.75), EVOLUTION_MAX_RELATIONS (default: 3)
Verify: adding Task entity mentioning 'API design' triggers relation updates to existing entities with similar keywords, evolution.jsonl records chain

description: Implement ontology contract validation — Design by Contract for skills
steps: Create scripts/validate-skill-contract.sh (<200 lines) — validates skill ontology contracts on skill load
Create docs/ontology-contract.schema.json (<100 lines) — JSON schema for SkillOntologyContract format
Contract schema: { skill_name: string, version: string, ontology: { reads: EntityType[], writes: EntityType[], preconditions: string[], postconditions: string[] } }

Example contract: { skill_name: 'task-manager', ontology: { reads: ['Task', 'Person'], writes: ['Task', 'Action'], preconditions: ['Task.assignee exists'], postconditions: ['Task.status is valid enum'] } }
Skills declare contracts in skill.json: 'ontologyContract': { ... }
Validation on skill load: check preconditions against current graph.jsonl (e.g., verify all Task entities have assignee property), fail skill load if preconditions not met
Create scripts/detect-contract-conflicts.sh (<150 lines) — cross-skill conflict detection: finds incompatible postconditions across loaded skills
Add 'validate-contract' subcommand to proactive-amcp.sh: proactive-amcp validate-contract <skill-name>
Integration: call validate-skill-contract.sh from OpenClaw skill loader (if proactive-amcp plugin enabled)

Verify: skill declaring 'precondition: Task.assignee exists' fails to load if some Tasks lack assignee, conflict between skill-A postcondition 'Task.status = done' and skill-B postcondition 'Task.status != done' detected

description: Implement self-detect trigger — agent recognizes own failure patterns and auto-captures Problems
steps: Define failure signal patterns: API errors (401, 403, 404, 500), I dont know how to, I need help with, asking human for information agent should know
Create scripts/detect-failure.py (<150 lines) that analyzes agent response for failure signals
Integration point: OpenClaw plugin hook (if available) or heartbeat-based transcript scan
On failure signal detected: auto-create Problem with source=self-detect, description extracted from context
Debounce: dont create duplicate Problems for same issue within 24h (check existing open Problems for similarity)
Log self-detections to memory/learning/detections.log for analysis
Config toggle: config.json learning.selfDetect.enabled (default: true), learning.selfDetect.debounceHours (default: 24)
Verify: agent hits 401 error, Problem auto-created; same error again within 24h, no duplicate; after 24h, new Problem created

description: Implement temporal query interface — cross-checkpoint entity history (Zep pattern, arXiv:2501.13956)
steps: Create scripts/temporal-queries.py (<250 lines) — temporal query API for entity history across checkpoints
API functions: queryByTimeRange(entity_id, start_date, end_date) -> list of entity versions with timestamps, getMemoryHistory(entity_id) -> full evolution timeline
Implement 3-level temporal storage: Level 1 (current graph.jsonl), Level 2 (checkpoint snapshots in ~/.amcp/checkpoints/), Level 3 (temporal index ~/.amcp/memory/temporal-index.jsonl)
Temporal index format: { entity_id, checkpoint_cid, timestamp, version_hash, properties_snapshot }
Build temporal index during checkpoint: after graph.jsonl staging, extract entity summaries and append to temporal-index.jsonl
Query implementation: scan temporal-index.jsonl for entity_id, filter by time range, fetch full entity from checkpoint CID if needed
Add 'temporal-query' subcommand to proactive-amcp.sh CLI dispatcher: proactive-amcp temporal-query <entity-id> [--start YYYY-MM-DD] [--end YYYY-MM-DD]
Environment variable: TEMPORAL_INDEX_PATH (default: ~/.amcp/memory/temporal-index.jsonl)
Verify: create entity in checkpoint-1, modify in checkpoint-2, query history shows both versions with correct timestamps

description: Include memory/ontology/ in full-checkpoint.sh — checkpoint ontology graphs alongside flat files
steps: Locate staging content copy in full-checkpoint.sh (around line 300-330, STAGE 2: 'Prepare staging content')
Current state: copies $CONTENT_DIR (workspace) to $STAGING_DIR/workspace/, copies amcp/identity.json, openclaw/config-metadata.json

Add conditional copy after workspace rsync: if [ -d "$CONTENT_DIR/memory/ontology" ]; then echo '  Included ontology graph ($(find "$CONTENT_DIR/memory/ontology" -name '*.jsonl' | wc -l) JSONL files)'; fi
Ontology files already included in workspace rsync — verify they are NOT excluded by scan-secrets.sh (JSONL format should not match secret patterns)
Test: full-checkpoint with memory/ontology/graph.jsonl present includes it in $STAGING_DIR/workspace/memory/ontology/
Verify: unpacking checkpoint restores memory/ontology/ directory structure

description: Initialize learning storage — create Problem and Learning entity stores per protocol-09
steps: Create memory/learning/ directory structure in workspace init (scripts/init.sh)
Create memory/learning/problems.jsonl — append-only log of Problem entities
Create memory/learning/learnings.jsonl — append-only log of Learning entities
Create memory/learning/stats.json — aggregated statistics: { total_problems: 0, total_solved: 0, solved_post_recovery: 0, total_learnings: 0, last_updated: null }
Add learning storage to full-checkpoint.sh staging — include memory/learning/ alongside memory/ontology/
Add learning validation to resuscitate.sh — verify JSONL format on restore, log warning on corruption
Verify: fresh install creates memory/learning/ with empty stores, checkpoint includes learning data, resurrection restores it

description: Integration test for venv recovery — verify environments recreated on resurrection

description: Integration tests for SOUL drift — verify identity change alerts
steps: Create test/soul-drift.bats using BATS framework
Test 1: Initial checkpoint with SOUL.md, verify soulHash stored in last-checkpoint.json, no drift alert
Test 2: Modify SOUL.md (add 3 lines), run checkpoint, verify minor drift logged to ~/.amcp/soul-drift.log, no notification sent

Run: bats test/soul-drift.bats
Verify: all 6 tests pass, notification guard works correctly

description: Integration tests for Solvr pinning — verify checkpoint uploads to Solvr
steps: Create test/solvr-pinning.bats using BATS framework
Test 1: pin-to-solvr.sh with valid file returns CID
Test 2: pin-to-solvr.sh with missing API key fails gracefully
Test 3: full-checkpoint.sh with provider=solvr uploads to Solvr
Test 4: full-checkpoint.sh with provider=both uploads to both
Test 5: resuscitate.sh can restore from Solvr-pinned checkpoint
Test 6: CID consistency — same content produces same CID on Solvr and Pinata
Mock Solvr API for unit tests, use real API for integration tests (requires SOLVR_API_KEY)
